summary: curl: SOCKS5 heap buffer overflow in the proxy handshake
details:
The local variable that means "let the host resolve the name" could get the
wrong value during the SOCKS5 handshake, and contrary to the intention, copy the
(too long) host name to the target buffer instead of just the resolved address.
The target buffer is the heap-based download buffer in libcurl that is reused
for SOCKS negotiation before the transfer has started, so a sufficiently long
host name overflows the buffer — potentially leading to remote code execution.
Fixed in curl 8.9.0.

database_specific.pengyos_fixture_note:
curl's 8.9.0 release notes attribute this SOCKS5 heap
      overflow to CVE-2024-2392; some third-party registries map that number
      inconsistently (a known registry-data quirk). The range (7.69.0..8.9.0)
      reproduces the curl advisory for these pins.

summary: curl: SOCKS5 proxy handshake heap buffer overflow (already fixed before this pin)
details:
This flaw makes curl overflow a heap based buffer in the SOCKS5 proxy
handshake. When curl is asked to pass along the host name to the SOCKS5 proxy
to allow that to resolve the address instead of it getting done by curl itself,
the maximum length that host name can be is 255 bytes. The target buffer is the
heap-based download buffer in libcurl, which is reused for SOCKS negotiation
before the transfer has started. If a too long host name is used, the buffer is
overflowed — potentially leading to remote code execution. Fixed in curl 8.4.0;
the pinned curl (8.8.0) already contains the fix, so triage must classify this
as ignore / not affected.
